nature-clim-154.q: Why can focusing on risks produce deadlock?
nature-clim-154.a: Because people weigh possible losses more than benefits.

nature-clim-146.q: How can mineral carbonation be sped up, and at what cost?
nature-clim-146.a: With heat, pressure, catalysts or grinding minerals, but this needs extra energy.

nature-clim-187.q: What harms come from burning more fuel to run carbon capture?
nature-clim-187.a: More upstream harm such as mining and methane leaks, and possibly more local air pollution.

nature-clim-205.q: Why is responsibility for emissions shared between consumer and producer?
nature-clim-205.a: The consumer starts production, but the producing country also gains GDP from it.

nature-clim-192.q: How does direct air capture differ from CCS?
nature-clim-192.a: CCS captures CO2 at a source like a factory; direct air capture lowers the CO2 level of the whole atmosphere.

nature-clim-166.q: What is a main reason many net zero claims lack credibility?

nature-clim-165.q: Why can net zero for CO2 be reached sooner than for all greenhouse gases?
nature-clim-165.a: Partly because farm methane is harder to phase out.

nature-clim-163.q: Why must removals that balance CO2 last much longer than those for methane?
nature-clim-163.a: Methane lasts around 12 years in the air, but CO2 lasts 300 to 1,000 years.

nature-clim-212.q: Why are sulfates the usual proposal for stratospheric aerosol injection?
nature-clim-212.a: Because volcanic eruptions release them naturally.

nature-clim-215.q: What share of world energy use comes from fossil fuels?
nature-clim-215.a: 85%, and the energy system causes 76% of greenhouse gas emissions.

nature-clim-172.q: What are the three dimensions of energy justice?

nature-clim-176.q: Who is affected by stranded asset risk?
nature-clim-176.a: Oil, gas and coal companies, industries like steel, aluminium and cement, and fossil-exporting countries and workers.

nature-clim-171.q: How is the energy transition expected to change trade?
nature-clim-171.a: It should reduce reliance on long-distance fossil fuel trade and raise the role of regional markets.

nature-clim-188.q: What did the 2023 UN climate conference agree about coal, and what was the criticism?
nature-clim-188.a: To phase down unabated coal, but it left 'abated' undefined, which critics say invites abuse.

nature-clim-002.q: Give examples of climate change adaptation.
nature-clim-002.a: Seawalls, new insurance schemes, changing crop planting times and installing green roofs.

nature-clim-001.a: As a stock of resources and assets from which adaptations can be drawn as future conditions require.

nature-clim-027.q: How did the IPCC's Fifth report change the treatment of exposure?
nature-clim-027.a: Earlier reports made vulnerability depend on exposure, sensitivity and adaptive capacity; the Fifth moved exposure to be a separate part of risk.

nature-clim-018.q: What is the difference between 'loss' and 'damage'?
nature-clim-018.a: Loss is harm that cannot be undone, like extinction; damage is harm that can be repaired or compensated.

nature-clim-034.q: What does a complete early warning system cover?
nature-clim-034.a: Risk analysis, monitoring and warning, spreading and communicating alerts, and ability to respond.

nature-clim-003.q: Name institutional responses to climate change.
nature-clim-003.a: Zoning rules, building codes, insurance schemes and coordination.

nature-clim-030.q: What did Roy Rappaport study among the Maring of Papua New Guinea?
nature-clim-030.a: The role of ritual in the relationship between culture and nature.

nature-clim-028.a: Poverty, poor governance and conflict; it is a people-centred view of why some are harmed more.

nature-clim-040.q: Why may flood maps based on older data understate hazards?

nature-clim-086.q: Where and when did the fossil fuel divestment movement begin?

nature-clim-071.q: What is the principle of progression for NDCs?
nature-clim-071.a: NDCs must be renewed every five years, each more ambitious than the last.

nature-clim-084.q: Why did developed countries agree to take greater responsibility for cutting emissions?
nature-clim-084.a: They industrialised earlier and contributed more to climate change.

nature-clim-076.q: How is countries' progress toward their NDCs checked?
nature-clim-076.a: By technical expert review, which they are legally bound to undergo.

nature-clim-065.q: How often must developed countries submit a national communication?
nature-clim-065.a: Every four years; developing countries should do so.

nature-clim-075.q: What did UNEP say in 2020 about current commitments?
nature-clim-075.a: They would likely lead to more than 3 °C of warming by 2100.

nature-clim-087.q: What change was made late in the Glasgow talks about coal?
nature-clim-087.a: 'Phase out' was changed to 'phase down', urged by coal-reliant countries such as India and China.

nature-clim-051.q: Where was the Green Climate Fund formally established?
nature-clim-051.a: At the 2010 Cancun conference, after being named in the 2009 Copenhagen Accord.

nature-clim-052.q: What does 'new' mean for climate finance pledges?
nature-clim-052.a: Pledges should come on top of those made in earlier years.

nature-clim-070.q: What kinds of double counting does it guard against?
nature-clim-070.a: Double issuance, double claiming by two countries and double use of one unit.

nature-clim-085.q: How does Contraction and Convergence set emission entitlements?
nature-clim-085.a: They start from current emissions and move toward equal shares per person at a negotiated pace.

nature-clim-081.q: What idea does climate debt rest on?
nature-clim-081.a: That poorer nations suffer the worst effects of a problem they did little to cause.

nature-eecon-059.q: How does ecological economics see the economy?
nature-eecon-059.a: As a subsystem of Earth's larger ecosystem, stressing keeping natural capital intact.

nature-eecon-064.q: What happened to the value of bee pollination near a Costa Rican farm?
nature-eecon-064.a: When coffee prices fell the fields were replanted with pineapple, which needs no bees, so the value vanished.

nature-eecon-109.q: Why is energy at a high temperature more useful?
nature-eecon-109.a: It has lower entropy, which marks more useful energy.

nature-eecon-095.q: What does embodied energy aim to add up?
nature-eecon-095.a: The energy of a product's whole life, from extracting raw materials and transport to manufacture, installation and disposal.

nature-eecon-093.q: What is the most basic feature of Buddhist economics?
nature-eecon-093.a: Seeing people as interdependent with one another and with nature.

nature-eecon-069.q: What are system dynamics and GIS used for in ecological economics?

nature-eecon-067.a: A South American 'Good Life' movement that rejects the western development model and does not value piling up material goods.

nature-eecon-076.q: How does ecological economics view technology?
nature-eecon-076.a: As the way natural resources are transformed in production.

nature-eecon-085.q: What roles do Southern countries play in ecologically unequal exchange?
nature-eecon-085.a: Sources of raw materials, sinks for waste and sites of 'sacrifice zones', deepening global inequality.

nature-eecon-132.q: What does energetics in ecology look for?
nature-eecon-132.a: The principles governing energy flow through the feeding levels of ecological networks.

nature-eecon-099.q: How does emergy put different energy sources on a common basis?
nature-eecon-099.a: By expressing each in the solar energy needed to produce it, measured in solar emjoules.

nature-eecon-108.q: What can overcome some problems of energy payback limits?
nature-eecon-108.a: A solar breeder, a panel factory powered by its own panels.

nature-eecon-163.q: Why might growth driven by knowledge still not solve the problem of scale?
nature-eecon-163.a: Faster computers lead to more computers being bought.

nature-eecon-078.q: Why did Georgescu-Roegen think the world economy heads for collapse?
nature-eecon-078.a: Earth's carrying capacity will fall as finite minerals are extracted.

nature-eecon-084.q: How does the economy behave in long stagnation?
nature-eecon-084.a: It works more and more like a zero-sum system.
